newsitem.title: USA: German carrier runs aground off Miami.
newsitem.headline: German carrier runs aground off Miami.

text.p: A German freighter loaded with butadiene ran aground in waters near Miami early Wednesday, but its cargo tanks were not damaged as it remained stranded for hours, the U.S. Coast Guard said.

The German-flagged bulk carrier Igloo Moon was transporting the chemical from the Middle East to Houston when it ran aground three miles (4.8 km) southeast of Key Biscayne, Fla., at around 5 a.m. EST (1000 GMT).

The Coast Guard said the ship's six cargo tanks had no apparent damage but that three fuel tanks on the starboard side were ruptured during the grounding. One of the tanks contained fuel, but a Coast Guard overflight of the vessel revealed no pollution.
The Coast Guard was nonetheless deploying a containment boom around the vessel as a precautionary measure and a three-mile (4.8-km) safety zone was established around the vessel.
A spokeswoman for the Coast Guard said she did not know who owned the vessel, but said a company she identified as ECM Hudson was representing them.
